title: How Do Domestic and Foreign Firms Respond to a Reduction in Competition from the Public Sector? Evidence from Vaccine Markets in India
authors: Arzi Adbi; Anant Mishra; Chirantan Chatterjee
eligible_reason: Single common shock: suspension of public-sector vaccine production licenses in January 2008 (revoked February 2010) applies to all treated vaccine markets at the same date. Regressions use period##treated (pre / during suspension / after revocation) with firm and market FE, season dummies and market-specific linear trends (c.timetrends##mkt) in every main column (Tables 3-6, Figures 4-5); Table 2 is a pooled OLS pre/post comparison. Not staggered, and unit-specific trends would exclude it anyway. Data (IQVIA) not shipped.
design_notes: Stata reghdfe lnrev/lnprod period##treated c.timetrends##mkt i.season, absorb(firmid mkt) vce(cluster firmid). Firm x market x month panel (45 firms, 31 markets, 144 months). Table 6 adds triple interactions with domesticfirm by political alignment.
data_files_note: README: commercial IQVIA India vaccine-sales data available by paid subscription; package contains only do files, logs, and graphs (do files load 'data', which is not shipped).
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text or PDF). Single-date shock with market-specific trends; no data shipped.
